mcqs.q: Which position holds that many religions can be valid paths to salvation or truth?
options: Pluralism
Exclusivism
Atheism
Fundamentalism

mcqs.q: Which question belongs to the study of social and historical developments?
options: How has the religion responded to the changing role of women?
Does the ontological argument prove God exists?
Is utilitarianism a hedonistic theory?
What are the four marks of mystical experience?

mcqs.q: What does the 'conflict thesis' about science and religion claim?
options: That science and religion are necessarily opposed - a view many historians dispute
That scientists must be atheists by law
That religion created modern science single-handedly
That science and religion ask identical questions

mcqs.q: Does secularisation mean religion is dying out everywhere?
options: Secularisation is a law requiring people to abandon religion.
Sociological data shows religion is in identical decline across the whole world.
All religions abolished their traditions in the twentieth century.
No - the thesis is contested: religion is growing in much of the global South, and some sociologists argue Western religion is changing form rather than simply declining.

mcqs.q: Have religions remained unchanged since their foundation?
options: No - constant development is the historical norm: schisms, councils, reform and revival movements have repeatedly reshaped every major tradition.
All religions abolished their traditions in the twentieth century.
Religions are frozen systems that have never changed since their founders.
No religious believer has ever worked as a scientist.

mcqs.q: Has religion always simply opposed science?
options: No religious believer has ever worked as a scientist.
No - the record is mixed: religious individuals and institutions have funded and pursued science (Mendel's genetics, Lemaitre's Big Bang theory), so the conflict thesis oversimplifies.
History shows religion fighting science at every turn.
Secularisation is a law requiring people to abandon religion.
